goal.decided: The accounting team prints each client's invoice, at that client's tax rate, from the invoice lines they keep in a spreadsheet, without asking a developer.

deliverables.name: The developers know who invoicer serves, the accounting team among them, and what each achieves with it

decisions.about: the roles besides the accounting team
decisions.decided: The developers who call invoicer as a library from their own code are a role besides the accounting team, and the library behavior they rely on stays as it is.

decisions.about: who installs the command for the accounting team
decisions.decided: A developer installs the command once for the accounting team, so installing belongs to the developer role; the accounting team never touches Python tooling, and the README tells them only how to run the command.

decisions.about: each objective with its role as subject
decisions.decided: O2 has the developers as its subject: they keep their own code giving the same results through each update of invoicer, without editing it. O3 states what the developer is left with in their own work: a command they install once and never need to set up again; printing stays O1's alone.

decisions.about: where each fact and name lives
decisions.decided: Roles says only who each role is and the part of the job they come for; the Concept alone says where the invoice lines come from and that the rate is set at each print; one name for each thing: invoice lines, and their own code.

decisions.about: the ranking of the key results
decisions.decided: The template's ranking paragraph, naming the first key results in the order KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 come first, then KR1.2, KR2.2 and KR3.2 in the order the document lists them; the template's sentence on no targets and Goodhart's law stays as the template writes it.

decisions.about: one objective for each piece of work
decisions.decided: The accounting team printing without a developer's help belongs to O1 alone; O3 counts only the developer's one install of the command; the one rounding of tax serves O2, as the library behavior developers rely on, and O1 takes its totals from it.

decisions.about: the concept: the one way and its ideas
decisions.decided: The one way: invoicer turns invoice lines into an invoice whose totals are right without anyone redoing the math. Its three ideas: invoice lines from the spreadsheet, for O1: the accounting team prints from the invoice lines they keep, and the command names any bad line and what's wrong; tax rate set at each print and never saved per client, for O1: the accounting team sets the tax rate anew for each invoice they print, so each client gets their own rate; same results for developers' own code, for O2: the command only calls the library, which rounds tax to the cent the same way every time. The install takes no idea.

deliverables.name: Someone in the accounting team learns from the README alone how to print an invoice from their spreadsheet lines at a client's tax rate
The developers build the invoice command's parts so that together they print what the README promises the accounting team
The developers see, before any body is written, that the invoice command's parts fit together with invoicer

The developers see, before the command is built, that its parts give the accounting team a printed invoice at each client's rate, and that the library calls developers rely on give what they gave before
The accounting team runs one command on their spreadsheet lines and gets the invoice printed at the rate they set
